n: Tax Refund and Identity-Based Benefit Fraud
ds: Offenders file false returns or benefit claims using stolen or fabricated identities and direct refunds to accounts they control. Banks see inbound refunds to unrelated accounts and mule behaviour.

src.t: IRS and HMRC public guidance on refund and identity fraud (general)
UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (specify year, e.g. 2025)

cn.rt: Fraudulent refunds and benefit payments landing in mule or stolen-identity accounts.

rat: Refunds/benefit payments landing in mule or prepaid accounts.

ind.n: Refund or benefit credited to account of different name
ind.cx: Payee name does not match the recipient listed.
ind.ds: Payment is requested to, or credited to, a personal, third-party or differently named account rather than the contracted payee.
ind.cn: Payment directed to personal or third-party account

ind.n: Multiple refunds into the same account
ind.cx: Unrelated refunds converge on one account or card.
ind.ds: Unrelated refunds converge on one account or card.

ind.n: Account holder surprised by refund or victim reports unexpected claim
ind.cx: Victim-side: customer discovers a fraudulent return in their name.
ind.ds: customer discovers a fraudulent return in their name.

ind.n: Recently opened account receiving government payments
ind.cx: New accounts used to receive claims.
ind.ds: New accounts used to receive claims.

ind.n: Rapid withdrawals or transfers after refund
ind.ds: A cheque deposit or refund is credited and quickly withdrawn or transferred before it clears or is verified.
ind.cn: Large credit followed by prompt withdrawals

ind.n: Application data shared across many claimants
ind.cx: Same device, IP or address in many claims.
ind.ds: The same device fingerprint, IP, phone, email or address appears across many applications, claims or apparent customers.
ind.cn: Shared device, contact or address data across many applicants or senders

ind.n: Income or dependants inconsistent with profile
ind.cx: Claim data diverges from account history.
ind.ds: Declared income, dependants or circumstances conflict with data held on the customer.
ind.cn: Claim details inconsistent with income, residency or account history

ctl.ds: Model that scores inbound-then-outbound pass-through, new-payee churn, counterparty diversity and profile mismatch to flag likely mule accounts. It prioritises accounts for review and restriction.

Checks the payee name against the destination account before release and warns on no-match or close-match, and flags payee-name mismatches against contracted entities. It interrupts misdirected, spoofed and fraudulent payments.

Requires refunds, cancellations and aborted-deal repayments to go back only to the original payer and method after validation of the request. It blocks the use of refunds to convert illicit funds into clean payments.

Matches accounts, devices, identifiers and beneficiaries against industry fraud sharing and ingests law-enforcement, commercial and open-source threat feeds, including victim reports from other institutions. It catches known bad actors early.
Rules that alert on abnormal count, value or speed of movements over defined windows compared with customer profile and peer norms. They provide baseline coverage across many typologies.
Tracks cases, outcomes, losses and false positives, routes concerns across fraud, sanctions and anti-corruption teams and feeds outcomes into tuning and appetite. It supports consistent handling.

Provides targeted messaging that helps customers recognise scam scripts and mule recruitment, verify requests independently and use trusted routes for giving or paying. It reduces victimisation and unwitting participation.

Remote verification of a person's identity using document capture, biometric matching and liveness or anti-spoofing checks, or a trusted digital identity. It reduces impersonation, synthetic identities and account opening with stolen or fabricated credentials.

ctl.n: Funds hold, freeze and recall procedure
ctl.ds: Provides a defined, legally grounded capability to restrict, hold, freeze or recall funds and accounts pending review or on confirmed exposure, with clear triggers and approvers. It stops onward dissipation of suspected illicit funds.

Fingerprints devices, IP addresses, emulators and network attributes to link applications, sessions and accounts and to flag shared or anomalous infrastructure. It exposes mule rings and multiple-account abuse.
Clusters customers, vendors and entities that share addresses, phones, devices, officers or bank details, including against staff records. It reveals common control and hidden relationships.

Independently verifies stated income, employment, obligations and application facts against third-party, bureau and prior-history data at origination. It reduces application, credit and insurance fraud.

Reviews and updates customer information on a risk-based cycle and when triggers occur, such as ownership change, key attribute change, adverse information or out-of-profile activity. Fresh data keeps risk ratings and expected-activity baselines current.
